name: ⛔ the inline-code exemption is removed, so a bare reference QUOTED as the wrong form fires — the one false positive the 21 measured firings actually contained
expect: ⭐ a bare #N inside INLINE CODE passes — a quoted counter-example, the one measured FP

name: the qualifier test is INVERTED, so a qualified reference fires and a bare one passes — the whole predicate backwards, which is the defect this guard exists to avoid
expect: ⭐ a BARE #N added to a spine doc is DETECTED

name: the ORDINAL allowance goes, so `Phase 6 #1` fires — the shape that was ~90% of the 2026-08-27 sample and the gap the self-test caught on its first run
expect: an ORDINAL in a title passes — the ~90% of the 2026-08-27 sample

name: the lookbehind goes, so a URL fragment and a `##4` heading are read as references — three false-positive shapes at once
expect: a URL fragment is not a reference

name: ⛔ scope goes UNCHECKED, so scripts/ comes back in — 87% of firings lived there and that is the axis the measurement chose
expect: ⭐ a bare #N in scripts/ is OUT of scope — 87% of firings lived there

name: a git failure returns an EMPTY diff instead of raising, so an unresolvable base is a silent PASS — the fail-open this repo's rc contract exists to refuse
expect: ⛔ an unresolvable base is CANNOT RUN, never a pass

name: docs/backlog.md drops out of scope again, so the file with the densest bare references is the one nothing reads — the premise that it 'owns the namespace' restored
expect: ⭐ a bare #N in docs/backlog.md is IN scope — PR numbers occupy the same integers

name: the roadmap drops out of scope, so a bare #N in the document that states what is left to do goes unread
expect: ...and the roadmap too, for the same reason

name: `deliverable` leaves the qualifier vocabulary, so a genuine qualified reference fires as a violation and the guard starts crying wolf
expect: `deliverable #2` is a QUALIFIED reference, not a bare one

name: #394: the marker-only exemption is never applied, so every retagged row's OLD references fire again
expect: #394: a MARKER-ONLY change to an existing row is exempt

name: #394: the comparison is LOOSE (same length, not byte-identical), so a changed word slips through
edits: return len(stripped) in {len(x) for x in same_file}
expect: #394: a marker plus ONE changed word is judged

name: #394: a marked line with nothing removed is exempt, so a NEW row escapes
expect: #394: a NEW row carrying a marker and a bare #N is judged

name: #394: any removal in a file exempts its unmarked added lines
edits:
if stripped is None:
        return False

if stripped is None:
        return bool(removed.get(path))
expect: #394: a removed line with no matching added line changes nothing

name: #394: the removed line may come from ANY file
expect: #394: the marker must match a line removed from the SAME file

name: #394: an invalid marker RAISES out of the gate instead of being judged
expect: #394: an INVALID marker on a changed line is still judged, never exempt and never a crash

name: #394: removed lines keyed on `+++ b/` again, so a DELETED file's lines are credited to the previous file (PR #442 r1 M1)
expect: #394: a line removed by DELETING another file never exempts a marked line (PR #442 r1 M1)
